title: Contract safeguard harness: golden prompts, automated contract assertions, and CI gates for streaming & tool calls
creator: Maya Chen
description: Build a lightweight, extensible test harness that runs golden-prompt regression checks and automated contract assertions for core API surfaces (streaming, function/tool calling, structured output). The harness should be runnable locally and as a step in CI, produce deterministic diffs against golden outputs, and provide actionable failure types (schema drift, tokenization changes, streaming chunking anomalies, tool-invocation shape mismatches). This ticket covers: definition of golden prompt vectors, assertion DSL for contracts, CI job integration (mandatory block on master), and a small pilot suite for 3 canonical endpoints.
acceptance_criteria: A harness executable (python/node script) that runs a set of golden prompts against the hosted dev runtime and writes a normalized diff report
CI pipeline includes a blocking job 'compatibility/golden-check' that fails the build on contract regression
Contract assertion DSL supports: required fields, type checks, order-insensitive arrays, and function-call shapes
Streaming tests detect chunk boundary regressions (missing chunks, reordered chunks, or truncated final chunk) and classify failures
At least 120 golden prompt vectors covering: 1) streaming chat, 2) function/tool calling with nested args, 3) structured JSON output with relaxed whitespace/ordering tolerance
Failure reports include a reproducible link + minimal prompt + expected/actual snippets and suggested rollback options
test_plan: Collect goldens: curate 120 prompt vectors from existing PRDs, customer repros, and internal evals; tag each with intent and strictness level
Implement assertion DSL as a small library (JS) used by harness and CI runner
Create normalization layer: canonicalize whitespace, JSON key ordering, and streaming chunk separators before diffing
Write adapters for: hosted API (staging), dedicated-local runner, and private VPC test endpoint
Add GitHub Actions workflow 'compatibility/golden-check' that runs fast (smoke subset) on PRs and full-suite nightly; block on master for full-suite failures
Run pilot: 3 endpoints (chat/stream, tools/function calls, structured-output) against runtime-1.22 on staging and iterate on false-positive tuning
implementation_notes: 2026-03-02: Initial spikes showed tokenization drift caused false positives for prefix-matching tests — adding normalization to compare token-aligned sequences
Decided to implement DSL in JS to re-use existing console/SDK utilities and to lower friction for front-end engineers
We will keep goldens and normalization rules in a separate repo 'compat-goldens' under org to allow reuse by Dedicated/Private test runners
Chosen CI approach: lightweight smoke on PRs (10 vectors) + nightly full suite (120 vectors) because full-suite on every PR is too slow for engineering velocity
Plan for rollouts: run full-suite for each runtime release branch and require zero critical regressions before promoting to canary
review_feedback: PM (Laura Kim): prefer clearer severity levels per vector (strict, tolerant, advisory) so customers can opt into strict mode
Design (Arjun Patel): add a dashboard link in the failure output that maps failing vectors to UX screenshots / reproduction steps
Security (Rina Das): verify goldens do not contain sensitive customer data; add a scanning pre-commit hook
SRE (Owen Murphy): include throttling and retry knobs for CI runner to avoid flapping when staging is degraded
linked_prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2046 - hydration fixes for streaming chunk markers
golden_prompt_examples: stream-chat: 'System: You are a helpful assistant. User: Stream numbers 1..N and stop after summarizing. Expected streaming chunks: ["progress:1","progress:2",...,"summary"] (strict)'.
tool-call-nested: 'User: Create calendar event with attendees as nested map; tool should be called with args {"title":string,"time":ISO8601,"attendees":[{"name":string,"email":string}] } (strict)'.
structured-json: 'User: Generate JSON inventory with keys sku, qty, meta (meta may be unordered). Accept any key order; numeric types must be integers (tolerant)'.
